purpose: State the portfolio-level viewpoint without transferring scientific ownership from source repositories.
central_question: Which distinctions become visible, necessary, identifiable, measurable, recordable, reportable, constrainable, realizable, actionable, or safely forgettable when the coordinate system, receiver set, architecture regime, niche representation, state/proxy measurement, record-entry process, observation contract, physical/ecological constraint grammar, future responsibility, retained mechanism set, sampling location, or report target changes?

novelty_claim.allowed: A portfolio-level viewpoint: ecological variation is treated as coordinate-, receiver-, architecture-, measurement-, record-, constraint-, evidence-, representation- and contract-relative state structure, while unresolved, negative, mixed, unavailable, censored and conflicting outcomes remain part of the scientific object. The repositories form one ecological research system through typed transfers of questions, evidence substrates, records, state claims and next-observation objects.
forbidden: one universal ecological state or mechanism already validated in nature
central synthesis ownership of source data, proofs, or primary claims
treating every visual connection as scientific dependency
treating shared substrate as shared conclusion
treating an ordered chapter programme as automatic evidence transfer

relation_rule: Scientific graph relations are typed. handoff, epistemic sequence, abstraction, provenance, complement, component, information flow and shared substrate are not interchangeable.

lenses.firewall: Changing coordinates, architecture, resolution, representation or receiver framing does not identify one causal mechanism or realized distribution.
Negative, mixed, sparse, censored, unavailable, failed-adequacy, non-identifiable or failed-generalization outcomes remain scientific objects rather than being rewritten as biological nulls.

Contract-relative compression is not arbitrary, intrinsic, universal, or automatically identified by current evidence; an empirical proxy must first earn endpoint-relevant status and preserve the distinctions it claims to encode.
